label: Everyday walking
description: Building a regular walk into your week — around the block, a park loop, or just further from the bus stop.
possible_benefits: May help you get a bit more daily movement in
Can be a low-pressure way to clear your head between tasks
beginner_steps: Pick one existing errand or habit to walk part of instead of ride
Try a 10-minute loop from your door and see how it feels
Notice one new thing on the route each time
time_cost_access: Free · 10–30 min · just a pair of comfortable shoes

label: Beginner run/walk plans
description: Structured plans that alternate walking and short jogs, designed for people who don't currently run at all.
possible_benefits: May build cardiovascular fitness gradually
Structured plans can reduce guesswork about pacing yourself
beginner_steps: Find a free beginner run/walk plan online
Do the first session at an easy, conversational pace
Rest at least a day between sessions at first
time_cost_access: Free plans available · ~20–30 min per session · running shoes recommended

label: Dance basics at home
description: Following short, beginner-friendly dance videos to move to music without any performance pressure.
possible_benefits: May be a playful way to enjoy music and movement together
No partner or class required to get a feel for it
beginner_steps: Pick one style that sounds fun (e.g. hip-hop basics, salsa steps)
Search for a 10-minute beginner tutorial
Do it once through slowly before trying it at speed
time_cost_access: Free · 10–20 min · open floor space

label: Chess fundamentals
description: Learning how the pieces move and a few opening ideas, then playing low-stakes games online or with friends.
possible_benefits: May give you a satisfying puzzle to chew on
Playing regularly can sharpen planning-ahead thinking
beginner_steps: Learn how each piece moves
Play a few games against an easy computer opponent
Learn one opening principle: control the center early
time_cost_access: Free to start · 15+ min per game · any device or a physical board

label: Logic puzzles & sudoku
description: Short daily puzzles — sudoku, crosswords, or logic grid puzzles — as a quiet mental warm-up.
possible_benefits: Can be a calm, focused break from screens full of notifications
May be satisfying without needing a big time commitment
beginner_steps: Pick one puzzle type to try for a week
Start with 'easy' difficulty even if it feels too simple at first
Keep a small notebook if you want to track ones you enjoyed
time_cost_access: Free · 5–15 min · pen and paper or a puzzle app

label: Starting a new language
description: Picking up basic phrases and vocabulary in a language you're drawn to, at whatever pace feels light.
possible_benefits: May be useful for travel or connecting with people
Short daily practice can build vocabulary steadily over time
beginner_steps: Choose a language and a free app or course
Learn 5 everyday phrases first (greetings, thanks, basic questions)
Practice out loud, even alone, for a few minutes a day
time_cost_access: Free tier widely available · 5–15 min/day · phone or laptop

label: Everyday sketching
description: Drawing small, low-stakes sketches of things around you — no talent requirement, just noticing shapes.
possible_benefits: May help you notice everyday surroundings differently
Low-pressure practice can build comfort with a pencil over time
beginner_steps: Get any notebook and pencil
Sketch one object near you for 5 minutes without erasing
Repeat with a different object tomorrow
time_cost_access: Cheap (paper + pencil) · 5–15 min · anywhere

label: Reflective journaling
description: Writing a few unstructured sentences about your day or thoughts — no audience, no formatting rules.
possible_benefits: Some people find writing things down helps them process the day
May be a private space to notice patterns in your thinking
beginner_steps: Pick a notebook or a plain notes app
Write 3 sentences about today, good or ordinary
Skip days without guilt — there's no streak here
time_cost_access: Free · 5 min · notebook or phone

label: Picking up an instrument
description: Trying a beginner-friendly instrument (ukulele, keyboard, or just your voice) with free starter lessons.
possible_benefits: May give you a creative outlet that doesn't require an audience
Learning a new skill step-by-step can be quietly rewarding
beginner_steps: Pick an instrument that's cheap or already in your house
Learn 3 basic chords or notes
Try playing along to one simple song
time_cost_access: Instrument cost varies (ukuleles are inexpensive) · 15–20 min · free tutorials online

label: Casual board game nights
description: Inviting a couple of people over (or joining a local group) for low-key board or card games.
possible_benefits: May be an easy, structured way to spend time with others
Games can take the pressure off 'small talk' as the main activity
beginner_steps: Pick one simple game you already own or can borrow
Invite 1-2 people for a casual evening
Keep the first one short — an hour is plenty
time_cost_access: Low cost · 1–2 hrs · a table and a couple of people

label: Local volunteering
description: Giving a small, occasional amount of time to a local cause you care about.
possible_benefits: May connect you with people who share your interests
Some people find a sense of purpose in contributing locally
beginner_steps: Think of one cause you already care about
Search for a local group or shelter that welcomes occasional help
Try a single short shift before committing to anything regular
time_cost_access: Free · a few hours, flexible · local availability varies

label: Interest-based local meetups
description: Finding a casual local group built around a specific interest, so conversation has a built-in topic.
possible_benefits: May make meeting new people feel less pressured, since there's a shared activity
Regular casual contact can help new interests stick
beginner_steps: Search for groups around one interest you already have
Read a couple of recent posts or reviews before going
Go once with no expectation beyond trying it
time_cost_access: Often free or low-cost · 1–2 hrs · local availability varies

label: Casual bird watching
description: Noticing and identifying birds you already see around your home or local park.
possible_benefits: May be a gentle reason to spend time outside
Some people find identifying things around them satisfying
beginner_steps: Sit somewhere outdoors for 10 minutes and just notice birds
Try a free bird identification app or field guide
Keep a simple running list of ones you've spotted
time_cost_access: Free (binoculars optional) · 10–30 min · a window or park

label: Container gardening
description: Growing a herb or vegetable in a pot on a windowsill or balcony — no yard required.
possible_benefits: May be a small, tangible project to check in on
Growing something you can eat can feel rewarding
beginner_steps: Pick one easy plant (basil, mint, or cherry tomatoes)
Get a pot, soil, and seeds or a starter plant
Water on a simple schedule and check in every few days
time_cost_access: Low cost · a few minutes every few days · pot + windowsill/balcony

label: Local trails & hiking
description: Exploring nearby trails or green spaces, starting with short, easy routes.
possible_benefits: May combine movement with time outdoors
Exploring somewhere new nearby can feel refreshing
beginner_steps: Search for an easy, short trail near you
Check weather and bring water
Go at an easy pace — this isn't a race
time_cost_access: Free or low-cost · 30–90 min · comfortable shoes

label: Beginner-friendly coding
description: Building small, visual projects with beginner coding tools rather than jumping into a full programming language.
possible_benefits: May give a concrete sense of how software is built
Small visible projects can feel satisfying quickly
beginner_steps: Try a beginner-friendly visual coding tool
Follow one short tutorial to build a tiny project (like a simple game)
Change one thing in the project and see what happens
time_cost_access: Free · 20–40 min · any computer

label: Beginner electronics kits
description: Trying a starter electronics kit to build a small circuit or gadget with step-by-step instructions.
possible_benefits: May be a satisfying hands-on way to learn how things work
Following clear steps to a working result can feel rewarding
beginner_steps: Find a beginner electronics kit with a guide
Set aside an evening with no distractions
Build the first small project exactly as instructed before experimenting
time_cost_access: Kit cost varies (often modest) · 1–2 hrs · table space

label: Intro to 3D printing
description: Downloading and printing a small pre-made design, before ever designing your own.
possible_benefits: May be a fun way to see an idea become a physical object
Browsing existing designs can spark other project ideas
beginner_steps: Find a place offering 3D printer access (library, makerspace, or a friend's printer)
Download one simple, small pre-made design
Watch it print before attempting your own design
time_cost_access: Access varies (libraries/makerspaces often free) · 1+ hr per print

label: Simple breathing exercises
description: A short, structured breathing pattern you can do anywhere when you want a brief pause.
possible_benefits: Some people find slow breathing helps them feel a bit steadier in the moment
Doesn't require any equipment or set-up
beginner_steps: Sit comfortably and breathe in for 4 counts
Hold gently for 4 counts
Breathe out slowly for 6 counts, repeat a few times
time_cost_access: Free · 2–5 min · anywhere

label: Gentle sleep routines
description: Small, realistic tweaks to your evening routine that may support easier winding down.
possible_benefits: A consistent wind-down routine may make it easier to settle at night for some people
Small changes are easier to sustain than a full routine overhaul
beginner_steps: Pick one small change (e.g. phone out of reach 20 min before bed)
Try it for a few nights without judging results too soon
Adjust based on what actually felt different, if anything
time_cost_access: Free · ongoing, a few minutes to set up · no equipment

label: Gentle stretching
description: A short daily stretch routine, focused on comfort rather than flexibility goals.
possible_benefits: May help you notice tension in your body
A short routine can be easier to actually keep up than a long one
beginner_steps: Pick 3 simple stretches (neck, shoulders, hamstrings)
Hold each gently for 20–30 seconds, never to the point of pain
Do it at a consistent time, like after waking up
time_cost_access: Free · 5–10 min · a bit of floor space
